notes:
I couldn't write the notes. My research tool stopped working before I could read a single page. My one attempt to fetch the sources came back with an error saying I had no more tool calls for this turn, so nothing reached me from Enduring Word, Bible Hub (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit), Precept Austin, NET Bible, New Advent or any other site.

You asked me to report only what the pages say, give a URL for every point and leave out anything I couldn't find. With nothing read, all that's left is my own memory, which you ruled out. So I'm not giving you any verse-by-verse notes, because I'd have no way to show they came from the sources.

When the tool is available again, this is what I'd read for each part of your request:

- **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word on Psalm 122; Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub; Precept Austin's Psalm 122 page; and Spurgeon's *Treasury of David* (spurgeon.org or Bible Hub/StudyLight).
- **Differences between traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), plus searches on Desiring God, Ligonier, The Gospel Coalition, GTY, 1517/LCMS and the Pentecostal sites. The questions I'd look at are:
  - How verse 1 applies to Christian worship and church-going
  - Whether "Jerusalem" in verses 3–5 means the church or Christ's kingdom
  - How verses 6–9 apply today
- **Other views:**
  - **NET Bible notes:** for verses 3–5.
  - **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine's exposition on New Advent, where it's numbered Psalm 121, and anything on catholic.com or oca.org.
  - **Popular modern teaching:** GotQuestions and similar pages on whether verse 6 promises prosperity to people who pray for or bless modern Israel. That's a debated popular claim, sometimes linked to prosperity teaching.

If you resend the request or tell me to try again, I'll start with those pages and write the notes in the format you asked for, citing only what each page actually says.
